title: Um fim de semana em Chicago

text.title: A Weekend in Chicago
paragraphs: Last month, Ana and her sister Bia visited Chicago for the first time. They [[booked]] a small hotel near the river and arrived on Friday night.

On Saturday morning, they walked [[along]] the lake for two hours. The weather was cold, but the [[view]] was amazing. In the afternoon, they visited an art museum and watched a short film about the history of the city.
In the evening, they tried a [[deep-dish pizza]]. Bia loved it, but Ana preferred her salad! After dinner, they listened to [[live]] jazz in a small bar. They stayed there until midnight.
On Sunday, it rained all day, so they stayed at the hotel. They played cards, talked and laughed a lot. Before they [[checked out]] on Monday, they planned their next trip: New York!

grammar.title: Past simple: verbos regulares
explanation: Usamos o past simple para ações que começaram e terminaram no passado. Ele aparece com expressões como yesterday, last weekend, last month e two days ago.
Nos verbos regulares, basta acrescentar -ed: walk → walked, visit → visited. E a forma é a mesma para todas as pessoas: I walked, she walked, they walked. Bem mais fácil que em português!

Atenção à ortografia: verbos que terminam em -e ganham só -d (arrive → arrived, love → loved). Consoante + y vira -ied (try → tried), mas vogal + y fica com -ed (play → played). Verbos curtos que terminam em consoante + vogal + consoante dobram a última letra (plan → planned, stop → stopped, prefer → preferred).
Na pronúncia, o -ed quase nunca é uma sílaba a mais: walked soa como "wokt" e played como "pleid". Ele só vira uma sílaba extra (/ɪd/) depois de t ou d: visited, wanted, needed.
O verbo to be é irregular no passado: I, he, she e it usam was; you, we e they usam were. Veremos outros verbos irregulares na próxima lição.
